headline: ASX snaps eight-day slide after Wall Street’s tech rebound
paragraphs: The ASX 200 broke an eight-session losing streak on Tuesday, closing 1.8% higher at 8,726. Technology shares rose 2.8%, and the gains spread across almost every sector. Energy was the exception, down 0.1% as crude oil stayed under pressure.

Wall Street set the pace on Monday. The S&P 500 closed up 4.7% at 7,237.17 and the Nasdaq-100 climbed 6.86% to 26,746.10. Nvidia’s decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive added to a rebound already under way in US stocks, with chip and AI shares leading the gains.
The Aussie dollar didn’t follow shares higher. The Reserve Bank’s Tuesday afternoon rate was 66.27 US cents, down from 66.38 on Monday.

Gold gave back an early gain: Reuters had spot gold up 0.1% at US$3,635.10 an ounce at 3:49 pm Sydney time, but GoldSquawk quoted it at US$3,626.05, down about 0.2%, at 5:03 pm. Brent crude futures were down 0.7% at US$88.71 a barrel at 4:10 pm as rising supply kept prices near three-month lows. These were intraday readings, not closing prices.
